verses.author: model_A
verses.text: A boat leaves the harbor before anyone is awake to see it go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light on anyway,
as if morning needed proof
that they meant to come back.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The tide keeps that promise longer
than most hands ever could,
carrying it back each dawn
folded small enough to hide.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I count the folds anyway,
not to check the math—
just to feel where the water pressed
a little longer than it needed to.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Some pressure leaves a mark
long after the hand has gone—
I've stopped calling that damage,
started calling it a way of staying.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Even the doorframe remembers
the height we stopped growing to—
a pencil line no one erases,
though the house has changed hands twice.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
New owners paint over the kitchen
but leave that one wall bare—
some marks arrive with instructions
even strangers know to keep.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A stranger's thumb finds the same worn spot
on the banister, without being told—
some grooves teach the hand
before the mind agrees to listen.
